summary: You present a clear coral-reef monitoring concept and cover most mission elements, with a logical report structure and STK access figures. The main limitation is that key orbit values and interpretations are inconsistent, weakening confidence in the design. Strengthen the technical evidence, clarify who operates the mission and who uses its data, and make your conclusions reflect what the analysis does—and does not—demonstrate.
next_steps: Rework the Orbit section using a consistent set of orbital elements: check the 600 km semi-major axis, use a retrograde inclination of about 97.8° for sun-synchronous precession, and explain how launch timing and orbital-plane geometry set RAAN. Verify the launch-site latitude and distinguish access duration from the number of daily contacts.

Build evidence that the mission will work: add payload resolution, swath and viewing geometry; a communications link budget and frequency/antenna compatibility; and a sized drag sail with a disposal-time analysis. Correct the interpretation of the 580.786-second access duration, and include relevant STK project files if available.

Revise the Introduction, Conclusion and presentation together: explicitly identify the operator and customer groups, qualify conclusions against the orbit and performance evidence, and check grammar, citation matching and bibliography quality. Replace unsupported or unsuitable references with appropriate sources.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction explains the coral-reef monitoring need, identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, and justifies using one spacecraft. To reach the next level, clearly name the mission operator and distinguish it from customer or user groups, with complete supporting references.
criteria.C2: Your Launch, Orbit and Ground Control & Communications sections cover the main design elements, and Images 1–5 provide STK access evidence. However, the stated 87.79° inclination cannot provide sun-synchronous precession; correct the orbit elements and support payload, link and EOL performance. Clarify access timing and provide the relevant STK files.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion usefully recaps the proposed design, but mostly summarizes it and presents consistent illumination too definitively. To reach the next level, draw specific conclusions from validated orbit and performance evidence, and identify limitations where the analysis does not establish mission capability.
criteria.C4: Your report has an Executive Summary, logical headings and a generally understandable structure. For a more professional standard, edit recurring grammar and wording issues, present the Bibliography consistently, and ensure every in-text citation matches a suitable listed source; the launch citations and Wikipedia reference need attention.
